translation

Marta Fogagnolo

To the Underworld Gods. Vipsanius Zotikos lived for 30 years. Herakleia (set this up) for her most devoted husband.

commentary

The epitaph was dedicated by his wife, Herakleia, to her husband, Vispanius Zotikos, who was probably a freedman of the gens Vipsania, whose members were well represented at Catania. This is unsurprising, as Vipsanius Agrippa owned estates in the area (see Salmeri 1984, 18–19), and is further confirmed by other Imperial-period funerary inscriptions mentioning individuals of the Vipsanii (IG XIV 494; IMusCatania 146; CIL X 2, 7101). The epitaph belongs to Formula G4 in Korhonen’s classification (2004, 86–87). It comprises an invocation to the gods — in the otherwise unparalleled abbreviated form ΘΚΔ, which represents a conflation of the formulae Θ(εοῖς) Κ(αταχθονίοις) and Θ(εοῖς) Δ(αίμοσι) (the instances in SEG 52.903 and 905 are antiquarian forgeries derived from this text) — followed by the name of the deceased and his age, the name of the dedicator, and the deceased’s name in the dative accompanied by an expression specifying the relationship between the two. The header is reported as complete and intact by Carrera and there is therefore no inherent reason to doubt it, although the abbreviation Κα(ταχθονίοις) is attested in ISic001152 from Termini Imerese and Carrera might have misread delta for alpha. The restoration proposed by Kaibel for line 5 (ap. IG XIV 495), εὐσεβ[εστάτῳ], is particularly convincing, since at Catania the superlative of εὐσεβής is attested exclusively in this type of funerary formula (cf. Korhonen 2004, 90).
